title: Winner margins, shared totals and linear rules
transcript: A margin is the difference between two scores. Use the smaller score as a base, then build the other scores by adding their margins. Put a label on each unknown before you use a symbol. As you work, keep the same label attached to the same quantity.

In AMC Upper Primary practice, look for shared totals with one score stated relative to another. A diagram or short equation can collect the clues in one place. In a Rossmoyne style puzzle, two or more conditions can constrain the same value. Substitute your result into the original conditions to prove it fits.
Two teams score forty-five points in total. The winner leads by seven. Find both scores. Imagine removing the extra points the winner has above the losing score.
Subtract the seven extra points. The remaining thirty-eight splits evenly between two equal parts. The two scores are nineteen and twenty-six. Restore the original margin to check.
The middle score is four above the lowest. The highest is six above the middle. Together the scores total fifty-three. Find the three scores. Take the lowest score as x.

The scores are x, x plus four, and x plus ten. The highest has both gaps above the lowest. Subtract the extras from the total and divide by three. The lowest score is thirteen. Add the margins back in order, giving thirteen, seventeen and twenty-three.
Teams A, B and C share eighty-four points. A leads B by five, and B leads C by fourteen. Give points from A and B to C so all scores become equal. How many points must each higher team give?

Write C as c. Then B equals c plus fourteen, and A equals c plus nineteen. Add the scores and subtract the extra amounts. This gives three c equal to fifty-one, so C has seventeen. The original scores were thirty-six, thirty-one and seventeen. The equal score is twenty-eight, one third of the fixed total.

A gives eight and B gives three. Subtract these from the first two scores and add both to C. All scores then equal twenty-eight. The total is still eighty-four, so this is the only possible equal score.

A winning margin measures how far ahead the winner is. It is not either team's score. When the same points move from one team to another, the shared total stays constant. Only its distribution changes.

Name the unknown quantity and write what each given relationship says about it. Label your equations with the units used in the story. Recheck the result by applying the original relationships, including each bound, whole-number rule or shared total.
